science.title: Curated peptide-HLA class I binding affinities with Rosetta structural ensembles
science.description: The interaction between peptide antigens and class I human leukocyte antigens (HLA) is a central determinant of CD8+ T cell recognition and a foundational target for cancer immunotherapy, vaccine design, and autoimmune disease research. Computational prediction of peptide-HLA (pHLA) binding has progressed rapidly with sequence-based machine learning, but structure-aware approaches remain limited by the scarcity of paired experimental affinity data and three-dimensional structural information. Here we describe a publicly released dataset combining curated quantitative binding affinity measurements from the Immune Epitope Database (IEDB) with computationally generated Rosetta FlexPepDock structural ensembles. The dataset spans 95 HLA-A, HLA-B, and HLA-C alleles, 25,622 unique peptides, and 112,561 peptide-allele pairs, each paired with a 25-decoy structural ensemble (2,814,025 decoy structures total, ~155 GB). We document the curation pipeline, the structure generation protocol, and two independent validation analyses to establish data quality. The resource is released under CC BY 4.0 on HuggingFace and is intended to support training and benchmarking of structure-aware pHLA binding affinity models.
